headline: Mandatory Interior and Vehicle Permits
reservation: A valid Ontario Parks permit is required for all vehicle entries and backcountry stays. Because Killarney is a premier destination, the George Lake campground and interior canoe routes often book out exactly five months in advance. Always confirm the current reservation window and check-in procedures at the George Lake office before heading into the interior.

days.title: The La Cloche Silhouette

stops.name: The Crack Trail
stops.detail: A challenging ascent through a massive rock fracture leading to views of the white quartzite mountains.

stops.name: O.S.A. Lake Access
stops.detail: Visit the lake that inspired the Group of Seven, known for its remarkably clear turquoise water.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes to reach trailheads from the park office; conditions vary.
days.note: The climb to The Crack involves steep rock scrambling; allow ample time before dusk.

days.title: George Lake and Granite Shores

stops.name: Chikanishing Trail
stops.detail: A coastal hike over pink granite ridges overlooking the North Channel of Lake Huron.

stops.name: George Lake Beach
stops.detail: The park's central hub for swimming and casual paddling beneath the quartzite ridges.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes between the village and the park entrance.
days.note: Coastal winds can make the Chikanishing area significantly cooler than the forest interior.

days.title: Killarney Village Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Killarney Mountain Lodge area

stops.name: Killarney East Lighthouse
stops.detail: A historic landmark marking the entrance to the narrow channel used by Great Lakes shipping.

stops.name: George Island Trail
stops.detail: Accessible via a short local boat shuttle, this trail offers a secluded look at local flora.

days.driving: Walking is suggested within the village; allow for local boat transfer times.
days.note: The boat shuttle to George Island is a local service and not operated by Ontario Parks.

intel.title: George Lake Trailhead
intel.text: The lot for The Crack is frequently full by early morning during autumn colors. Utilize the designated overflow areas only as directed by park staff to avoid fines.

intel.title: Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect total signal loss once you descend into the valleys between the La Cloche ridges. Do not rely on mobile apps for navigation in the backcountry.

intel.title: Highway 637 Gap
intel.text: The stretch between Highway 69 and Killarney Village has no fuel stations. Ensure your tank is full before leaving the Sudbury or Parry Sound corridors.

intel.title: Seasonal Bug Activity
intel.text: Black fly and mosquito levels are peak in June and can impact hiking speeds. Suggested travel times are faster in late August when pests subside.

intel.title: Interior Canoeing
intel.text: Access to interior lakes like Bell and David requires specific entry-point permits. Verify that your rental provider is permitted to deliver to these remote locations.

plan.arrival: Arrive from Sudbury via Highway 637; pick up heavy groceries in Sudbury as village selection is limited. Check in at the George Lake gatehouse for all permits.
plan.vehicle: Cars are fine for Highway 637, but the road to Bell Lake is gravel and can be washboarded; check rental agreements for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Killarney East Lighthouse provides an unobstructed view of the Georgian Bay horizon.
